note: Conforming and non-conforming documents under §a.14 as of v1.7: a document ends at the closing --> of its last block, with at most one trailing line ending (LF, CRLF or a lone CR). These exist because three independent implementations read v1.6 identically and identically wrongly — agreement between implementations was no evidence, since it came from the same sentence. A shared answer file is the fix: implementations compare against these cases instead of against their own reading. The last case pins the §a.13/§a.14 interplay: an archive-timestamp block is a block, and a boundary check that does not recognise its marker reports a valid archive layer as tampering.
